name: DJ Jazzy Jeff / A Touch of Jazz
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 neo-soul — DJ Jazzy Jeff / A Touch of Jazz
notes: The Philadelphia **production house** that supplied Jill Scott, Musiq Soulchild, Jaguar Wright and Raheem DeVaughn their board — Carvin & Ivan, Dre & Vidal and Keith Pelzer are all its graduates, and the entry says to "model this as a **house preset** that the individual producer entries specialise". The window is 1994–2008 per Gate 2; the 1986–89 Fresh Prince era is excluded by the entry itself. The drums are the house grammar: "a programmed kick/snare base with the backbeat hard on 2&4, a **live hat or ride played over the top**, swung 16ths, ghost snares, and a continuous congas/shaker layer". The programmed-under-live split is the jitter map — kick 3 ms and snare 4 against a closed hat at 11 — and the ride sits in the percussion lanes with the congas and shaker at 4–7 hits a bar. "Turntable scratches are used as a percussion voice and as a transition device (the house's founder is a battle DJ)", which is the extra `perc` lane and the instrumental break in the arrangement. Harmony is "**jazz harmony over a hip-hop grid** — extension-rich 4-to-8-bar cycles from a played keyboard, with cadences and bridges, so it sits harmonically closer to jazz than to radio R&B of the same years": a triad weight of 0.08, chord durations of 2–8 beats and a harmonic rhythm that moves. Bass is "played electric bass with walking, chromatic-approach motion; no sustained 808". The whole-song production habit — "not beat placements" — is the full arrangement with a prechorus and a bridge. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum number and all melody figures; the research documents the house's role and its graduates and marks the parametric detail as inference from the catalogue. ⚠ Its three graduate models in this section share this grammar by design; they specialise it at their own numbers rather than restating it.
